senses.gloss: (b. h.) to exist; to be, become; to occur, come to pass.—With part. ה׳ מביט he looked; ה׳ אומר he said, freq. used to say.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:11">Gen. R. s. 1</cite>, beg. <he>אני הָיִיתִי וכ׳</he> I was the implement &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:6">Ib.</cite> <he>ה׳ הקב״ה מביט וכ׳</he> the Lord looked into the Law (as often as a thing was to be created).
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:13">Ab. I, 13</cite> <he>הוא ה׳ אומר</he> the same used to say.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 2:4">Gen. R. s. 2</cite> <he>ה׳ ללמה ולא כלום</he> became a nothing; a. v. fr.—Apocopate forms: <he>אֱהִי</he>, <he>אֱהֵא</he>, <cite ref="V00123"><he>תְּהִי</he></cite>, <cite ref="V00114"><he>תְּהֵא</he></cite>, <cite ref="J00139"><he>יְהִי</he></cite>, <he>יְהֵא</he>; <cite ref="V00117"><he>תְּהוּ</he></cite> (= <he>תִּהְיוּ</he>), <he>יְהוּ</he> (= <he>יִהְיוּ</he>).

<cite ref="Yoma 66b:3">Yoma 66ᵇ</cite> <he>אהא בשלום אני נכ׳</he> (<cite ref="Tosefta Yoma 4:6">Tosef. ib. IV</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Yoma 3:14">III</cite>), 14 <he>נִהְיֶה</he>) may I and you be as well; Y. ib. VI, 43ᶜ bot. <he>כן תהו וכ׳</he> so may ye be well.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 35a:11">B. Mets. 35ᵃ</cite> <he>תהא במאמינו</he> let this be (speak of a case) when he accepts his opponent’s statement; a. v. fr.—Part. <he>הוֶֹה</he>, <he>הוֶוֹה</he>

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 6:6">Sabb. VI, 6</cite> <he>דברו חכמים בה׳</he> the scholars (in using the words ‘Arabian women’) speak of the ordinary custom (not to the exclusion of other people); a. fr.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 11:1">Pesik. R. s. 11</cite>, end <he>הם הווִֹים ודומים</he> [<he>להקב״ה</he>] they shall be existing for themselves (not merely as an attachment) and resembling [the Lord]; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 11:1">ib.</cite> <he>אף הם הווים אש וכ׳</he> they, too, shall endure as a consuming fire.—

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:13:4">Cant. R. to II, 13</cite> <he>עניות ירבה ויוקר הווה</he> (read <he>תרבה</he>) poverty shall increase, and prices remain high (different in <cite ref="Sanhedrin 97a:4">Snh. 97ᵃ</cite> a.
Sot. 49ᵇ, v. אָמַר II). Imper. הֱוֵי, הֱוֵא; pl. הֱווּ.
Ib. II, 3; a. fr.—הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר, also elliptically הֱוֵי say, i.e. you must admit, this proves, that is meant by saying.
<cite ref="Taanit 2a:10">Taan. 2ᵃ</cite> which is the service of the heart? <he>ה׳ אומר זו תפלה</he> you must admit, it is prayer.
<cite ref="Tosefta Niddah 1:6">Tosef. Nidd. I, 6</cite> <he>ה׳ לא אמרום וכ׳</he> that is to say, the scholars have spoken &c.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6:4">Cant. R. to I, 6</cite> <he>ה׳ כרמי שלי וכ׳</he> this is meant by ‘my vineyard &c.’—Y. Shebu. VII, 38ᶜ top <he>הווי לא צורכה וכ׳</he> it is evident that it would not have been necessary &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to change one’s legal status, to dispose of.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 40b:13">Keth. 40ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>תהיה</he> <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:19">Deut. XXII, 19</cite>) <he>במְהַוָּה עצמה וכ׳</he> the text speaks of a woman who can dispose of herself.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 58a:7">Kidd. 58ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>והיית</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 7:26">Deut. VII, 26</cite>) <he>כל שאתה מְהַיֶּיה הימנה</he> whatever thou makest out of it; <cite ref="Temurah 30b:22">Tem. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>מְהַיֶּה ממנה</he>; a. e.
